reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Convening committees, councils, and boards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and all source notes (L. 1965 p. 391 § 1 through A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; dual effective dates 8-28-13 and 10-11-13 after H.B. 650 veto override; and footnote ** noting '28 U.S.C. 206' in original rolls versus '23 U.S.C. 206**' in body). Covers DNR's responsibility to convene any committee, council, or board it deems necessary or advisable for state parks, historic sites, trails, outdoor recreation, chapters 253 and 258 federal grants, Land and Water Conservation Fund Act, or other laws; source federal-citation discrepancy retained without silent repair. Independent review revised title to remove unstated "advisory" qualifier because subsection 1 covers any committee, council, or board DNR deems necessary or advisable; retained original-rolls federal-citation discrepancy ("28 U.S.C. 206" vs. "23 U.S.C. 206**") and H.B. 650 veto-override note.

headings.title: Department staff support and office space
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes (including H.B. 650 veto-override note). Distinguished from subsection 1 by addressing DNR's obligation to provide all staff support and office space for any committees, councils, or boards convened under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections and all source notes, and verified all source, transcript, and subsection fingerprints. Checked DNR convening and staffing duties, the 2013 H.B. 28 / H.B. 650 dual effective dates (8-28-13 and 10-11-13 after veto override), and footnote ** recording "28 U.S.C. 206" in original rolls versus "23 U.S.C. 206**" in the body (retained without silent repair). Revised subsection 1 to remove the unstated "advisory" qualifier; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Inter-Agency Council Fund creation and federal deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1965 p. 391 § 8, A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; H.B. 650 effective 10-11-13 following veto override). Covers creation of The Inter-Agency Council Fund in the state treasury for DNR use and deposit of federal moneys received under the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965, Public Law 88-578.

headings.title: Appropriated outdoor recreation uses and local allocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Covers appropriation prerequisite, restriction to outdoor recreation planning, acquisition, and development (noting the archived source's repeated phrase 'for outdoor recreation for outdoor recreation planning'), minimum fifty-percent allocation to Missouri political subdivisions, and prohibition on using locally allocated moneys for projects supervised or controlled by a state agency.

headings.title: Nonreversion of balances and section 33.080 exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Covers retention of unexpended balances at the end of an appropriation period without transfer to general revenue and express exemption from section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and all source notes, and verified all source, transcript, and subsection fingerprints. Checked Inter-Agency Council Fund creation, LWCF Public Law 88-578 deposits, appropriation prerequisite, minimum 50% political-subdivision allocation, section 33.080 nonreversion, 2013 H.B. 28 / H.B. 650 veto-override dual effective dates, and the source body's duplicated phrase "for outdoor recreation for outdoor recreation planning" in subsection 2. Confirmed all three drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Definition of trail and nonstate trail conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1669 § 1 through A.L. 2004 S.B. 810). Covers the section-specific definition of 'trail' for state and political-subdivision public hiking, biking, or recreational trails, plus mandatory designation, conveyance-purpose statement, exclusive-design, and non-road/non-sidewalk exclusions for trails not acquired by the state. Independent review revised title from "local trail qualifications" to "nonstate trail conditions" to match statutory phrasing ("a trail not acquired by the state") and cover both mandatory designation/conveyance/design conditions and road, street, and sidewalk exclusions.

headings.title: Conditional immunity for trail-adjoining landowners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Covers immunity from civil liability for injuries to persons or property of trespassers or unpermitted entrants on trail-adjoining land, conditioned on both entry by way of the trail and subsequent injury on adjoining lands. Independent review revised title to mark immunity as conditional on trespass or unpermitted entry, entry via the trail, and subsequent injury on adjoining land.

headings.title: Exceptions for intentional, unlawful, willful, or wanton acts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by stating when immunity under this section does not apply: injuries caused by an owner's or possessor's intentional, unlawful, willful, or wanton act.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections (including subdivisions) and history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked section-specific trail definition, political-subdivision designation/conveyance/exclusivity conditions, road/street/sidewalk exclusions, conditional trespasser-injury immunity, and subsection 3 exceptions for intentional, unlawful, willful, or wanton acts (distinct from 258.200(2), which also excludes negligent acts). Revised subsections 1 and 2 for exact statutory scope and conditionality; retained subsection 3.

headings.title: Conditional immunity for stream- and river-adjoining landowners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), history note (L. 2000 H.B. 1097 § 258.110), and source footnote (*Word 'person' appears in original rolls for 'persons*'). Covers immunity for landowners adjoining navigable or nonnavigable free-flowing streams or rivers against injuries to trespassers or unpermitted entrants, conditioned on entry via the stream or river and subsequent injury on adjoining lands; original-rolls discrepancy retained explicitly. Independent review revised title to mark immunity as conditional on trespass or unpermitted entry, waterway entry, and adjoining-land injury, matching 258.100(2); retained original-rolls footnote ("person" vs. "persons*").

headings.title: Exceptions for intentional, unlawful, negligent, willful, or wanton acts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 (and from 258.100(3)) by excluding immunity when injuries are caused by the owner's or possessor's intentional, unlawful, negligent, willful, or wanton act.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections (including subdivisions), history note, and original-rolls footnote (*Word "person" appears in original rolls for "persons*"), and verified all fingerprints. Checked conditional stream- and river-adjoining landowner immunity and verified subsection 2's express exclusion of negligent acts alongside intentional, unlawful, willful, or wanton acts (contrasting with 258.100(3)). Revised subsection 1 to reflect conditional scope; retained subsection 2.
